tools.name: search_events
tools.title: Search registry events
tools.description:
Search BORME registry events (since 2009) across companies by publication
date, province, act type and company name, newest first.

Use it for questions about many companies ("insolvency notices in Valencia
in September"). For one known company use company_history; to find a
company use search_companies; for one day's totals use daily_digest.

Returns JSON {count, events: [{event_id, date, borme_id, province,
company_name, company_slug, acts: [{act_type, act_type_raw, roles,
payload}], registral}]}, plus company_name_match, plan_window and
hidden_by_plan when they apply. No next page: when count equals limit,
narrow the filters.

Read-only; one request per call against your daily quota. Without an API key
(X-API-Key header, https://bormeapi.com/account) only the last 7 days
are searched (plan_window). An empty page with hidden_by_plan means
matches exist outside your plan's window: do not say none exist. A bad
date, province or act type is refused with a message naming the fix.

date_from.title: Date From
date_from.description: Earliest publication date, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-09-01. Optional; data starts on 2009-01-02. Without a key it is moved up to 7 days ago (plan_window says so).

date_to.title: Date To
date_to.description: Latest publication date, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-09-30. Optional; defaults to the latest day held.

provinces.title: Provinces
provinces.description: Optional list of BORME province names, accent- and case-insensitive, e.g. ["MADRID", "CADIZ", "VIZCAYA"]. An autonomous community stands for all of its provinces, e.g. ["Basque Country"] or ["Cataluña"]. Full list: the resource borme://provinces.

act_types.title: Act Types
act_types.description: Optional list of act type enums; an event matches if it has any of them, e.g. ["INCORPORATION"] or ["INSOLVENCY_DECLARATION", "INSOLVENCY_STATUS"]. Full list: list_act_types. Barcelona prints some acts as free text under "Otros conceptos": recognised wording gets its own act type (act_type_raw stays "Otros conceptos"; fields.shareholder names a sole shareholder when the text does), and a same-entry revocation and reappointment becomes RE_ELECTIONS. Reprocessed events keep their event_id, but their acts can change.

company_name_contains.title: Company Name Contains
company_name_contains.description: Optional part of the company name, case- and accent-insensitive, e.g. "mercadona"; use at least 3 letters or digits for a selective search. % and _ match literally. It filters events; to look a company up by name, call search_companies first.

tools.name: company_history
tools.title: Company registry timeline
tools.description:
Get one company's BORME timeline: its published registry events within your
plan's window.

Use it once the company is known (a slug from search_companies or
company_by_nif); across many companies use search_events. A name instead
of a slug is searched: several matches return {ambiguous: true,
candidates}, none returns {error}.

Returns JSON {company_slug, total_events, first_seen, last_seen, truncated,
next_offset, count, events} (as in search_events), with former_slugs for
a merged company (an old slug returns the merged timeline) and
plan_window on a limited plan. total_events, first_seen and last_seen
cover the whole timeline in your window, not just this page. To page,
keep limit and order and pass next_offset as offset (at most 10000)
until it is null.

Read-only; one request per call. Without an API key (X-API-Key header) only
the last 7 days; basic covers 365 days, pro and risk the full history
back to 2009. If all its events are outside your window, the refusal
counts them.

company.title: Company
company.description: Company slug, e.g. vaz-metales-sl (from search_companies), or a name of at least 3 letters or digits, e.g. "Mercadona", searched case-insensitively.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Events to skip, integer 0-10000 (default 0); pass the previous page's next_offset, e.g. 100.

order.title: Order
order.description: "desc" (default, newest first) or "asc" (oldest first), e.g. "asc" to start from the earliest event in your plan's window.

tools.name: company_by_nif
tools.title: Find a company by NIF
tools.description:
Look up a Spanish company by its NIF/CIF tax ID. Use it when the user gives
a tax ID (with a name use search_companies); on a hit, call
company_history with the company_slug.

Returns JSON {found, company_slug, company_name, current_name, status,
province, nif_source, nif_caveat, ...}; use current_name. BORME has no
dedicated tax-ID field: there are more than 580,000 NIF mappings from
public sources and the text of BORME notices, covering a minority of
companies, so a miss (reason nif_unmapped) means "not matched yet", not
"does not exist". invalid_input true: not a NIF/CIF. reason
nif_check_character_failed: wrong check character; relay tell_the_user
and the did_you_mean candidates. reason not_registry_entity: explain
entity_type as the note does. ambiguous true: ask which candidate.
nif_caveat present: say the link is not settled.

Read-only; one request per call. Needs the basic plan or higher: send your
API key in the X-API-Key header (https://bormeapi.com/account).

nif.title: Nif
nif.description: Spanish NIF/CIF, normally 9 characters, e.g. B12345674. Spaces, hyphens, dots and the ES VAT prefix (ESB12345674) are accepted; other country prefixes are not.

tools.name: brand_owner
tools.title: Find a brand's company
tools.description:
Find the Spanish company a trademark or trading name is linked to, in the
Spanish patent office's (OEPM) trademark and commercial-name records we
hold (the archive starts in 1987).

Use it when the user names a brand; for a company's own name use
search_companies, for a known company's brands use company_brands.

Returns JSON {found, brand, matches: [{brand, kind, company_slug,
company_name, company_status, file}], truncated, source, note}. kind
commercial_name identifies a business; trademark distinguishes goods or
services (NESCAFÉ is not another name for Nestlé): say which kind a hit
is. Links come from holder-name matching (the office publishes no tax
IDs); ambiguous holders stay unlinked: present a hit as a name match,
not confirmed ownership. found false is not proof the brand is unused.
On a hit, use company_history with the slug.

Read-only; one request per call. Needs the basic plan or higher: send your
API key in the X-API-Key header (https://bormeapi.com/account).

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: Brand or trading name, or part of it, at least 3 letters or digits after punctuation is removed, case-insensitive, e.g. "ZARA".

tools.name: company_brands
tools.title: A company's brands
tools.description:
List the trademarks and trading names that the Spanish patent office (OEPM)
records under a holder with this company's name.

Use it for a known company (a slug from search_companies or
company_history); to go from a brand to its company use brand_owner.

Returns JSON {company_slug, commercial_names, trademarks (each {name, file,
status, since}), counts, truncated, limit_per_kind, source, note}. The
office publishes no tax IDs, so every link is a name match, not
confirmed ownership. An empty result means none is linked in our data,
not that the company holds none. limit applies to each kind separately,
newest first; counts is what this answer lists, not the company's total,
and truncated true for a kind means more are linked: raise limit.

Read-only; one request per call. Needs the basic plan or higher: send your
API key in the X-API-Key header (https://bormeapi.com/account).

company.title: Company
company.description: Company slug, as returned by search_companies or company_history, e.g. vaz-metales-sl.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum results per kind (trademarks, trading names), integer 1-200, e.g. 10 (default 50).

tools.name: recent_signals
tools.title: Recent risk signals
tools.description:
Get a sample of the latest risk signals derived from BORME and public
sources: at most 10 rows dated within the last 7 days.

Use it for "what risk signals appeared this week"; not a per-company check
(use company_history) and not the full feed (the hosted API's
/v1/signals).

Returns JSON {count, window, sample_cap, signals: [{signal_type, date,
company_slug, company_name, province, details}], full_feed}. AEAT_DEBTOR
comes from the AEAT's yearly debtors list (art. 95 bis LGT): details
carry listed_on, list_year, is_current_list (true for 12 months from
listed_on) and debt_eur, the published total at 31 December of the prior
year. Say the company was on the list published on that date; never say
the debt is still outstanding. count 0 means none in the window, not
that a company is risk-free; an unknown signal_type is refused with the
valid list.

Read-only; one request per call. Needs the risk plan: send your API key in
the X-API-Key header (https://bormeapi.com/account).

signal_type.title: Signal Type
signal_type.description: Optional, one of INSOLVENCY_FILED, ACCORDION, MASS_EXIT, OWNERSHIP_CHANGE, DISTRESS_COMBO, PHOENIX, ADDRESS_CLUSTER, AEAT_DEBTOR, PUBLIC_CONTRACT_AWARD, e.g. MASS_EXIT; omit for all types.

tools.name: daily_digest
tools.title: Daily BORME digest
tools.description:
Summarise one BORME publication day: total events, counts by act type, the
top 10 provinces and the day's insolvency-proceedings notices.

Use it for "what was published today" or a day's figures; to read the
notices use search_events with date_from = date_to = that day.

Returns JSON {date, total_events, by_type, top_provinces, insolvencies:
[{company, province}]}. insolvencies lists the events with
INSOLVENCY_DECLARATION or INSOLVENCY_STATUS (not SUSPENSION_OF_PAYMENTS,
BANKRUPTCY_LEGACY or PROVISIONAL_SHEET_CLOSURE_INSOLVENCY). An
INSOLVENCY_STATUS notice can record any stage, from a request for a
declaration to the conclusion: before saying a company was declared
insolvent, read the act's payload with search_events. A day without a
gazette (weekends, holidays) returns total_events 0.

Read-only; one request per call. Without an API key only days within the
last 7 days; send your key in the X-API-Key header
(https://bormeapi.com/account) for your plan's window.

date.title: Date
date.description: Publication day, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-10-27; omit for the latest day in the database.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.title: Search companies by name
tools.description:
Find Spanish companies by name and return ranked company cards. Use it first
when the user gives a company name, then company_history with its
company_slug; with a tax ID use company_by_nif, with a brand use
brand_owner.

Matches current names, former names and variants, ignoring accents, case,
punctuation and the legal form. Returns JSON {query, count, total,
total_is_at_least, truncated, limit, offset, companies: [{company_slug,
name, legal_form, province, municipality, status, in_insolvency,
last_act_date, match, matched_on}]}. match is exact, prefix, contains or
fuzzy (a lead, not an identification; say so). Ranked by match, then
active companies, then newest act.

Read-only; one request per call; not limited by the free plan's 7 days of
history. The free plan shows at most the first 5 ranked cards;
hidden_by_plan counts the rest: relay its note. The NIF is on the card
from the basic plan up (X-API-Key header). An empty answer is not proof
that a business does not exist.

name.title: Name
name.description: The bare company name or part of it, at least 3 letters or digits and at most 200 characters, e.g. "inditex" or "Talleres Jarama": no city, parentheses or notes. Matching allows for case, accents and punctuation, and a legal form such as SL or SA can be left out. Do not repeat the same query unchanged after an empty answer: read note and hidden_by_plan if present.

province.title: Province
province.description: Optional province, accent-insensitive, e.g. MADRID or VIZCAYA, or an autonomous community for all of its provinces, e.g. Catalonia; several values separated by commas, e.g. BIZKAIA,GIPUZKOA. Applied to the candidates the search reads (2,000 with a filter), so a broad name can return fewer companies than match it.

status.title: Status
status.description: Optional, one of active, dissolved, extinct, sheet_closed, e.g. active; applied like province.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Cards to skip, integer 0-200 (default 0), e.g. 10. At most 200 cards are ranked; truncated true means a candidate cap was reached or a search step ran out of time, so add another word from the name.

tools.name: list_act_types
tools.title: List act types
tools.description:
List every normalized BORME act type: the enum used by the act_types filter
of search_events (act_type), its Spanish label (spanish) and its English
label (english).

Use it to choose act_types values or to translate act types in an answer; it
reads no registry data. Returns a JSON array of {act_type, spanish,
english}, sorted by act_type. Read-only, open to everyone, no key needed
and not counted against a quota. The same list is the resource
borme://act-types.

tools.name: registry_stats
tools.title: Data coverage and freshness
tools.description:
Report the coverage and freshness of the BORME data behind this server.

Use it to answer "how much data is there?", "how fresh is it?" and "can I
trust date filters for period X?" before running searches; it says
nothing about any one company.

Returns JSON {events_approx, companies_approx, coverage: {from, to},
parse_completeness_last_30d, source}: approximate event and company
counts (planner estimates, not exact tallies), the first and latest
publication day held (YYYY-MM-DD), and the event-weighted parse
completeness over the 30 days up to the latest run (e.g. 0.9987). Takes
no arguments. Read-only, open to everyone, no key needed and not counted
against a quota. The same report is the resource borme://coverage.

arguments.description: Company name, slug (e.g. vaz-metales-sl) or NIF/CIF (e.g. A28015865).
arguments.name: company

prompts.description: Due-diligence brief on one Spanish company from the notices published in BORME: identification, published history, officer appointments and their later changes, and insolvency and status notices, each act cited with its BORME id, within your plan's history window. Uses search_companies or company_by_nif, then company_history.
prompts.name: company_due_diligence
prompts.title: Company due diligence

arguments.description: Company name or slug, e.g. "Mercadona" or vaz-metales-sl.
arguments.name: company

arguments.description: Earliest publication date to cover, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2025-01-01; leave empty for the company's whole history within your plan.
arguments.name: since

prompts.description: Appointments, re-elections, terminations and resignations, revocations and ex officio cancellations of appointments of the directors and other officers of one Spanish company, from the notices published in BORME, optionally since a date, each change cited with its BORME id. Uses search_companies, then company_history.
prompts.name: board_changes
prompts.title: Board changes

arguments.description: BORME province or autonomous community, e.g. MADRID, VIZCAYA, Catalonia.
arguments.name: province

arguments.description: Publication day, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-10-27; leave empty for the latest day in the database.
arguments.name: date

prompts.description: Companies whose incorporation notices were published in BORME on one day, for one Spanish province or autonomous community, with name, slug and BORME id, from search_events (act type INCORPORATION). Without a date, uses the latest publication day (daily_digest).
prompts.name: new_companies_digest
prompts.title: New companies digest

arguments.description: NIF/CIF, a letter and 8 characters, e.g. B12345674; spaces, hyphens, dots and the ES prefix are accepted.
arguments.name: nif

prompts.description: Check a Spanish NIF/CIF tax ID against the BORME API's company-to-NIF links: the company linked to it in this data, any format or check-character problem the tool reports, and the linked company's latest published acts. Uses company_by_nif (Basic plan or higher), then company_history.
prompts.name: check_nif
prompts.title: Check a NIF

resources.description: Every normalized BORME act type: the enum used by the act_types filters (act_type), its Spanish label (spanish) and its English label (english). The same list as the list_act_types tool. Open to everyone.
resources.name: act-types
resources.title: BORME act types

resources.description: The 52 province values BORME prints (Ceuta and Melilla among them), each with the spellings listed for it, plus Spain's autonomous communities and the autonomous cities, each with the names it accepts and the province values a filter on it covers. The same list as GET /v1/provinces. Open to everyone.
resources.name: provinces
resources.title: BORME provinces and autonomous communities

resources.description: How much BORME data this server holds and how fresh it is: approximate event and company counts (estimates), the first and latest publication day held, and the share of gazette text structured (weighted by events) over the 30 days up to the latest processed day. The same report as the registry_stats tool. Open to everyone.
resources.name: coverage
resources.title: BORME data coverage and freshness

resourceTemplates.description: Up to 20 of the most recent published events of one company, by slug (e.g. vaz-metales-sl, as returned by search_companies), with total_events, first_seen and last_seen: the same answer as company_history with company set to the slug, limit 20 and order desc, under the same plan rules (without an API key, the last 7 days only) and counted as one request. For more, call company_history.
